newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH PSE REJECTS CBANK AGROBANKA TRADING REQUEST.
newsitem.headline: CZECH PSE REJECTS CBANK AGROBANKA TRADING REQUEST.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange on Thursday said it had rejected a request by the central bank to halt trading in shares of troubled bank Agrobanka a.s. on the bourse's free market.
"After a thorough examination...the (PSE) General Secretary has decided to not accept the application," the PSE said in a statement.
The PSE statement added that the bourse could not pull an issue off of its free market just because it was experiencing basic economic difficulties.
In September, Agrobanka, the fifth largest bank, went into forced administration because of low liquidity connected to the failure of a smaller Plzen-based bank, Kreditni Banka a.s..
The central bank is currently searching for a majority shareholder to take control of Agrobanka which was connected to Kreditni through an obscure investment firm called Motoinvest.
The central bank made the request through its administrator.

Last week the central bank set out its plan to revive Agrobanka, the country's fifth largest bank, by splitting the troubled institution's sound and questionable assets to allow the entry of a strategic investor.

The central bank said it was splitting the bank's assets into two parts -- questionable and sound -- allowing for the sound assets to be sold off in a tender while the questionable assets will be retained and "their value realised".
